catalog_quote: 4. Acento prosódico. Las raíces de las palabras de clase mayor se acentúan. El acento prosódico tiene un efecto en la pronunciación de las vocales en ciertos contextos (véase Convenciones). ... [§5] Una vocal modal acentuada es fonéticamente laringalizada, un poco alargada, y seguida por una breve oclusiva glotal con soltura, cuando se presenta en posición final de la frase: / m á / [ ˈm á̰ ˑ ˀ ă̰ ] ma ‘animal’ ... Los pronombres enclíticos y los demostrativos enclíticos no se acentúan y por lo tanto esta oclusiva glotal no se presenta con ellos ... [§1] El zapoteco de Santa Catarina Quioquitani tiene raíces monosilábicas, a diferencia de otras variantes de la región que preservan las raíces bisilábicas del proto-Zapoteco ... [§3] Se presentan tres tonos fonémicos superficialmente: Alto, Bajo y Ascendente (Bajo-Alto).

new_statements.translation: [p. 6] "4. Prosodic stress. The roots of major-class words are stressed. Prosodic stress has an effect on the pronunciation of vowels in certain contexts (see Conventions)." [p. 7] "Enclitic pronouns and enclitic demonstratives are not stressed, and therefore this glottal stop does not occur with them" [p. 1] "Santa Catarina Quioquitani Zapotec has monosyllabic roots, unlike other varieties of the region that preserve the bisyllabic roots of proto-Zapotec (Fernández de Miranda 1995). The loss of the second (unstressed) syllable of proto-Zapotec has produced a series of palatalized consonants"

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for this language has an empty rule; this work supplies one (root stress, monosyllabic roots, unstressed clitics, plus three-way tone). Nothing in the catalog is contradicted. Note the listed open_url (SIL archive 29557) is the Vocabulario landing page, not this item; the correct open copy ishttp://lengamer.org/publicaciones/trabajos/zapoteco_de_Quioquitani_afi.pdf,the URL the PDF itself prints in its running footer.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the root of every major-class word; roots are monosyllabic (the unstressed second syllable of proto-Zapotec roots has been lost), so the stressed syllable is the root syllable, and prefixes (e.g. possessive /ʃ-/ with epenthetic /i/, aspect prefixes) and enclitic pronouns/demonstratives are unstressed. All phonetic transcriptions in the sketch place the stress mark [ˈ] on the root syllable (e.g. /ʃìkpàj/ [ˈʃ ì k p à j]? -- transcriptions such as [ˈʃpǐˑd̥ má] xpid ma, [ˈʃnítʲ tʲ] xnijty, [ˈlԑ̀ˑ mé] lë me consistently stress the root and leave the enclitic unstressed). Stress has phonetic effects: a stressed modal vowel is laryngealized, slightly lengthened and followed by a brief glottal stop phrase-finally; unstressed enclitics lack this. The language is also tonal: three surface tones, High, Low and Rising (Low-High), contrastive on the root vowel (§3, p. 5). The label 'tone language with a stress statement' is the alternative reading; 'morphologically determined' is chosen because the work states a placement.
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitic pronouns and enclitic demonstratives are unstressed (p. 7). The brief non-syllabic 'vowel' produced by a prefixed /w-/ before a consonant is ignored by speakers when humming, whereas 'los hablantes generalmente no ignoran las vocales no acentuadas' (p. 6), so words like wxidzy, wyee, wto count as monosyllabic.
new_statements.identity_note: Both works describe the variety of Santa Catarina Quioquitani itself (ex-distrito de San Carlos Yautepec, Oaxaca), Michael Ward's fieldwork 1983-1996; the 2008 sketch's recordings and text are from co-author Emiliano Zurita Sánchez, born 1967 in Santa Catarina Quioquitani. The sketch states that ISO code ztq also covers the very similar variety of Santa Catalina Quierí and, per INALI, San Pedro Leapi, Santiago Lachivía, Santo Domingo Lachivitó, Santo Tomás Quierí and San Baltazar Chivaguela; the stress statement is made for the Quioquitani variety only.

tone_statements.quote: 3. Tonos. Las lenguas zapotecas son tonales. Hay tres tonos superficiales contrastantes en tiits së: alto, bajo y ascendente (bajo-alto). Los ejemplos se presentan en Ward, Zurita Sánchez y Marlett (2008). Los tonos no se marcan ortográficamente en los trabajos publicados, pero hay personas que sugieren la inclusión de algunos tonos escritos [...] [§4.7 Tonos] El tono bajo y el tono alto descienden un poco antes de una pausa. [...] [Apéndice B] Tonos: Se identifican tres tonos: alto, bajo y ascendente (bajo-alto).
tone_statements.translation: 3. Tones. The Zapotec languages are tonal. There are three contrastive surface tones in tiits së: high, low and rising (low-high). Examples are given in Ward, Zurita Sánchez & Marlett (2008). Tones are not marked orthographically in published works, but some people suggest including some written tones [...] [§4.7 Tones] The low tone and the high tone fall a little before a pause. [...] [Appendix B] Tones: three tones are identified: high, low and rising (low-high).
tone_statements.locator: §3 'Tonos', p. 5; §4.7 'Tonos', p. 6; Apéndice B 'Consonantes, vocales y tonos', p. 7
tone_statements.summary: 3 contrastive tones: H, L, rising (LH), on monosyllabic roots, cross-cut by modal vs laryngealized vowels; H and L drift down pre-pausally; tone unmarked in practical orthography.

sources.note: Community orthography note: citing the SIL 'Ilustraciones fonéticas' chapter (Ward, Zurita Sánchez & Marlett), it restates that Quioquitani Zapotec has three phonemic tones, high, low and rising (low-high), each occurring on modal (simple) and laryngealized (double) vowels, and counts 'seven' categories (3 tones x 2 phonations plus words whose vowel 'se pronuncia como en español' that the author cannot assign to a tone). It proposes carrying the illustration's diacritics into everyday writing: acute accent for high tone, circumflex (replacing the illustration's breve) for rising tone, and NO…
